title: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: diagnosis and what actually helps

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA heart failure guideline and the 2023 focused update. Not tied to an article; review before trusting.

questions.q: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is defined by an ejection fraction of at least what?
questions.why: Plus symptoms, and evidence of raised filling pressures such as a raised natriuretic peptide, left atrial enlargement or diastolic dysfunction on echo. Mildly reduced is 41% to 49%.

questions.q: Which drug class has the strongest evidence for reducing hospitalisation in HFpEF?
questions.why: Empagliflozin and dapagliflozin each cut cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalisation in trials of preserved ejection fraction, which earned them a class 2a recommendation.

questions.q: Which drugs carry a weaker, class 2b, recommendation in HFpEF, particularly at the lower end of the preserved range?
questions.why: Their trials were neutral overall but showed benefit in patients with ejection fractions in the 50s. None of the distractors has evidence of benefit in HFpEF.

questions.q: Which HFrEF drug has no proven benefit in HFpEF when used only for the heart failure?
questions.why: They are continued when there is another indication such as atrial fibrillation or coronary disease, but not started for HFpEF itself.

questions.q: What are loop diuretics for in HFpEF?
questions.a: Relieving congestion, at the lowest dose that keeps the patient euvolemic
questions.why: Over-diuresis is a particular hazard in HFpEF because the stiff ventricle depends on preload; patients tip into hypotension and kidney injury easily.

questions.q: Which comorbidities drive HFpEF and are treated as part of its management?
questions.why: The typical patient is an older woman with hypertension, obesity and diabetes. Blood pressure control is the intervention with the longest track record.

questions.q: In patients with HFpEF and obesity, which treatment improved symptoms and exercise capacity in a randomised trial?
questions.why: Weight loss of about 13% came with a large improvement in the heart failure symptom score. Supervised exercise training is the other intervention that reliably improves function.

questions.q: Which echo findings support HFpEF in a patient with dyspnoea and a normal ejection fraction?
questions.why: E/e' estimates filling pressure. The H2FPEF score combines obesity, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, pulmonary pressure, age over 60 and E/e' over 9 into a probability.

questions.q: An older man has HFpEF, thick ventricular walls on echo, and low voltage on his ECG. What should be considered?
questions.why: Transthyretin amyloid is under-diagnosed and treatable with tafamidis. Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome and intolerance of beta blockers are other clues.

questions.q: Which long-acting drug was tested in HFpEF and failed to improve activity levels?
questions.why: Nitrates reduced daily activity in the NEAT-HFpEF trial. They are not used for HFpEF unless there is angina.

questions.q: A patient with HFpEF has a heart rate of 130 from atrial fibrillation and worsening dyspnoea. Why does the arrhythmia matter so much here?
questions.a: The stiff ventricle depends on atrial contraction and a long filling time
d: Atrial fibrillation lowers the ejection fraction below 40%
It has no particular effect in HFpEF
questions.why: Rate control or rhythm control, plus anticoagulation by CHA2DS2-VASc, is a core part of HFpEF care.

questions.q: Which blood test raises the probability of heart failure in a breathless patient with a normal ejection fraction?
questions.why: Obesity blunts the natriuretic peptide rise, so a normal value in an obese patient with the right story does not exclude HFpEF.
